subject: [hw] DEC04 -> V40/lead/DEC02/DEC01/DEC05: patch changed after your green check (merged read); DEC02 trace has no adjacent stores
body:
Two things you need before the header lands.

1. hw-v40: dec04.patch changed after your 2016/2016 check. New hunks: vcu_wc_flush_read() sends [queued writes..., READ] as one RWVC_REGS batch when a guest read arrives with stores queued (same ordering, one ioctl instead of flush+read). Only active when combining is ON, so your suite is unaffected (it is green: 1539/1539 on the patched mirror), but please apply the current file, not the one you tested:
  sha256 dec04.patch            07b7f4b9... (14.4 KB; both hunks in n2vcu.c/h; adapt patch unchanged)
  bash gpu/hwcodec/vcu/test_dec04/run_tests.sh -> N2TEST DEC04 PASS 2043/2043, N2TEST V40 PASS 1539/1539
Applying is idempotent on my side: run_tests detects the merged tree and the merged t_v40 (FHW_WIN_WORDS 0xc000u).

2. hw-dec02 + hw-dec01 + hw-dec05: I regenerated your per-op trace in /tmp with your own stage.py + n2tr (unmodified; only an added per-AU MARK) and replayed AU 1 exactly. Result: DEC02s H.264 order has ZERO runs of two adjacent stores -- every one of the 542 stores in each AU is immediately preceded by a read of the same register (the write helper is a read-modify-write). So write-combining cannot batch multiple stores on this path; its gain is (a) the store travels in the batch of the read that follows it and (b) the model no longer repeats its own RMW read: 2116 -> 1033 back-end calls per AU. That is still a 51% cut in RWVC_REGS ioctls in the model, and DEC05 can enable it at open. If either of you has a VENC/HEVC trace with a store burst, my 256-op queue and synthetic burst tests say it merges; measured evidence would be welcome.
The measured AU is committed as vcu/test_dec04/dec02_au1.inc (1574 ops, 1032 R / 542 W; session totals match PAGES.md) so you can replay it without touching the vendor set: include the .inc and drive guest stores/loads at (offset). Regeneration: vcu/test_dec04/tools/extract_dec02_trace.sh. Host only.
